niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, markets, creative needs, measurement demands, and whether you want programmatic, direct buys, or both. Below is a practical way to think about choosing one and a short list of top players to consider.

How to choose (key criteria)
- Inventory access: premium streaming apps, Roku/Hulu/OTT publishers, and walled-garden platforms (Roku, Samsung, Amazon).  
- Buying approach: programmatic DSP vs. direct/publisher deals vs. a mix.  
- Measurement & attribution: cross-screen unified measurement, deterministic/identity solutions, viewability/completes.  
- Targeting & data: first-/second-party data activation, household targeting, deterministic TV IDs.  
- Creative capabilities: CTV-specific creative, interactive/video-first formats, dynamic creative.  
- Transparency & reporting: open auction vs private marketplace, fee structure, granular reporting.  
- Vertical experience & case studies: evidence of results in your industry (ecommerce, CPG, auto, B2B, etc.).  
- Scale & geography: local vs. national vs. international reach.

Agencies / platforms to consider (by strength)
- The Trade Desk — leading programmatic DSP with strong CTV buying, data integrations and cross-screen planning. Best if you want programmatic scale and advanced targeting.  
- Roku/OneView — first-party access to Roku inventory and robust measurement; great for reaching large Roku audiences and running platform-native buys.  
- Samsung Ads — premium access to Samsung smart TV audiences and deterministic TV IDs; strong if you want household-level reach on Samsung sets.  
- Cadent (Comcast Advertising) — access to Comcast/NBCUniversal inventory and addressable CTV solutions; good for premium publisher ties and linear+CTV planning.  
- VideoAmp — cross-platform measurement and planning (TV + streaming), strong for ROI-focused optimization across linear and CTV.  
- Innovid — creative + ad serving + measurement for CTV; good if you need dynamic/interactive CTV creative and unified reporting.  
- Amobee — end-to-end platform for TV, CTV and digital, including data and measurement integrations.  
- Tremor Video / Magnite / SpotX — major programmatic video supply or SSPs (sell-side), often used by agencies for inventory access; good partners if you need broad publisher reach.  
- Simulmedia — specialty in audience-based TV and CTV planning; useful for marketers wanting coordinated linear + streaming strategies.  
- Media/holding groups — large global media agencies (e.g., OMD, Mindshare, Starcom, Wavemaker, MediaHub) provide full-service strategy, creative, buying, and measurement across screens — good if you want an integrated global solution.

How to pick one quickly
1. Define KPIs (awareness, reach/frequency, lower-funnel ROI, installs, purchases).  
2. Ask for case studies in your vertical, measurement approach, and specific publisher access.  
3. Run a short pilot (30–60 day) with clear success metrics before scaling.  
4. Insist on transparency (inventory, fees, viewability, reporting cadence).

If you tell me your business (vertical), budget range, target geography, and primary KPI, I can recommend the top 2–3 agencies/platforms to evaluate and suggest sample RFP questions or a pilot plan.
